case.C01.title: Burning budget on broad match
case.C01.summary: The campaign runs on broad match with an almost empty negative keyword list. Clicks arrive, but most come from searches that will never buy.
case.C01.symptoms: Spend is normal or high, but lead quality is low. The search terms report shows 'free', 'jobs', 'course' and competitor names; observed CPA is rising.
case.C01.hint: The search terms report shows which queries burn money. Look at what was actually clicked first, then narrow the scope.
case.C01.correct.outcome: You reviewed search terms and added negatives. Within a week or two irrelevant spend dropped, volume shrank a little and CPA improved.
case.C01.wrong.outcome: Raising budget, waiting, or shutting everything down did not fix it. Irrelevant clicks kept eating money, or the good traffic vanished too; cash eroded.
case.C02.title: Learning-limited ad sets
case.C02.summary: A small budget is split across many ad sets and none collects enough events to finish learning.
case.C02.symptoms: Ad sets show 'learning limited'. CPM and CPA swing day to day and delivery is uneven.
case.C02.hint: Splitting data slows learning. Concentrate budget in few ad sets and avoid frequent edits.
case.C02.correct.outcome: You merged ad sets and cut edits. Delivery stabilised and CPA fell over time.
case.C02.wrong.outcome: Opening more sets or changing bids and audiences daily kept resetting learning; costs stayed erratic.
case.C03.title: Creative fatigue
case.C03.summary: The same ad has been shown to the same small audience for too long and people are tuning it out.
case.C03.symptoms: Frequency climbs, CTR drops, CPM is flat or rising. Comments turn negative and CPA creeps up.
case.C03.hint: As frequency rises the same budget buys fewer results. You need fresh creative and a wider audience.
case.C03.correct.outcome: You added new variants and widened the audience. CTR recovered and cost per result fell.
case.C03.wrong.outcome: Only raising budget or narrowing the audience pushed frequency higher; results per spend got worse.
case.C04.title: Platform over-reporting
case.C04.summary: Ad platforms each claim the same conversions. Reports look great but little money reaches the bank.
case.C04.symptoms: Platform CPA looks excellent while paid customers in the CRM are few. Channel reports sum to more than the CRM shows.
case.C04.hint: Platforms overstate their own contribution. Use the CRM as the reference and test incrementality.
case.C04.correct.outcome: You used the CRM as the reference and measured incrementality with a holdout. Budget shifted to genuinely incremental channels.
case.C04.wrong.outcome: Scaling on platform ROAS blew up marginal CAC; cash melted while the reports still looked good.
case.C05.title: Conversion loss from consent management
case.C05.summary: The consent banner changed and a big share of conversions became invisible. Customers still arrive but the platform cannot see them.
case.C05.symptoms: Observed conversions dropped suddenly while spend and clicks stayed the same. Smart bidding lowers bids and volume collapses.
case.C05.hint: A real loss and a measurement loss are different things. Check the CRM and recover signal the lawful way.
case.C05.correct.outcome: You set up server-side tracking and CRM feedback. Signal partly recovered and bids returned to normal.
case.C05.wrong.outcome: You shut the campaign down as 'not working' or removed the consent banner: you either lost volume or took on legal and reputation risk.
case.C06.title: Policy violation and account restriction
case.C06.summary: The ad copy or landing page contains an unsupported claim. The platform rejected the ads and account health dropped.
case.C06.symptoms: Ad disapprovals, an account health warning and delivery stopping. The appeal takes days.
case.C06.hint: Read the disapproval reason, fix the content, then appeal. Trying to dodge the rules loses the account for good.
case.C06.correct.outcome: You read the reason, fixed the content and appealed. After a short outage the ads came back.
case.C06.wrong.outcome: Resubmitting the same ad or opening a workaround account got you permanently suspended; you lost your main channel.
case.C07.title: Tracking tag breaks
case.C07.summary: After a site update the conversion tag broke. Customers keep coming but the algorithm went blind.
case.C07.symptoms: Observed conversions fell to near zero, clicks are normal and the CRM still gets leads. Bids drop within days.
case.C07.hint: Verify and fix the tag first. Feeding the algorithm a wrong signal costs more than the broken tag itself.
case.C07.correct.outcome: You fixed the tag and restored conversions from the CRM. A short dip, then recovery.
case.C07.wrong.outcome: Manually changing bids or pausing and rebuilding the campaign poisoned the algorithm; learning reset and weeks were lost.
case.C08.title: Competitor price cut
case.C08.summary: A competitor cut prices or launched a free plan. Trial users now ask why you cost more.
case.C08.symptoms: Trial-to-paid falls, price objections rise, and competitor brand searches and CPC climb.
case.C08.hint: Do not walk blindly into a price war. Lead with value and local strengths, and protect existing customers.
case.C08.correct.outcome: You sharpened positioning and protected existing customers. Losses stayed limited and margin held.
case.C08.wrong.outcome: Matching the discount at once crushed margin and LTV; outspending them with ads stretched payback.
case.C09.title: Seasonal swing
case.C09.summary: Search volume and leads dropped but the campaign is fine; the season changed.
case.C09.symptoms: Search volume and leads fluctuate, CPC shifts and existing customers use the product less.
case.C09.hint: Tell campaign problems from seasonality using last year's data. Do not mistake a season for the new normal.
case.C09.correct.outcome: You adjusted expectations for the season and focused on retention in the slow period; cash stayed smooth.
case.C09.wrong.outcome: You tore up a healthy campaign in the low season, or spent as if the peak was permanent; cash got tight.
case.C10.title: Onboarding failure and churn
case.C10.summary: Trials convert to paid but customers leave in months 2-3. They cannot set up or use the product.
case.C10.symptoms: Early-cohort churn is high, usage is low and support tickets rise.
case.C10.hint: Do not keep filling a leaky bucket. Define activation and invest in the first week.
case.C10.correct.outcome: You defined activation and added a first-week call. The cohort curve lifted and LTV grew.
case.C10.wrong.outcome: Buying more customers or blaming the season collapsed LTV/CAC while MRR stalled.
case.C11.title: CAC blow-up from over-scaling
case.C11.summary: You raised budget fast. Average CAC creeps up, but the marginal cost of the latest spend is very high.
case.C11.symptoms: Marginal CAC passes the LTV threshold, frequency rises, quality falls and runway shortens.
case.C11.hint: Watch the marginal, not the average. Raise budget gradually and spread across channels.
case.C11.correct.outcome: You tracked marginal CAC and raised budget gradually. Growth stayed sustainable.
case.C11.wrong.outcome: Doubling budget because 'ROAS was fine' blew up marginal CAC and shortened runway.
case.C12.title: Negative review crisis
case.C12.summary: An outage or bad experience piled up negative reviews and trust in brand searches wavered.
case.C12.symptoms: Reputation falls, rating drops, trial starts decline and support load grows.
case.C12.hint: Reply fast, openly and respectfully, and fix the problem. Never fake reviews.
case.C12.correct.outcome: You replied quickly, fixed the problem and asked real customers for reviews. Reputation recovered gradually.
case.C12.wrong.outcome: Arguing publicly or faking reviews brought platform sanctions and a reputation collapse.
case.C13.title: Payment and tax surprise
case.C13.summary: An unexpected tax bill and payment processor deductions pushed cash below expectations.
case.C13.symptoms: Collections trail MRR, payments fail, a tax bill arrives and the cash buffer is thin.
case.C13.hint: Part of revenue is not yours. Set aside a tax reserve and track failed payments.
case.C13.correct.outcome: You reserved for tax and set up dunning. The surprise shrank and runway held.
case.C13.wrong.outcome: Ignoring tax and spending without a buffer cut runway suddenly.
case.C14.title: Cold outreach legal trouble
case.C14.summary: Cold email, SMS or calls without permission brought leads short-term but complaints followed. This is game commentary, not legal advice.
case.C14.symptoms: Replies and leads rise first; then complaints, spam flags, damaged domain reputation and a possible regulatory warning.
case.C14.hint: Permission-based lists, opt-out and each market's rules are essential. Rules differ widely by market.
case.C14.correct.outcome: You switched to permissioned lists, opt-out and warm intros. Slower but safe.
case.C14.wrong.outcome: Scaling volume or buying a list brought penalties, reputation damage and lost email deliverability.
case.C15.title: PMax inflated by brand traffic
case.C15.summary: Performance Max shows ads to people already searching for you and credits itself.
case.C15.symptoms: PMax CPA is great but total new customers do not grow; brand searches are booked to the campaign.
case.C15.hint: A great CPA may just count people who were coming anyway. Exclude brand and look at total CRM.
case.C15.correct.outcome: You excluded brand and ran a holdout. The true incremental contribution emerged.
case.C15.wrong.outcome: Piling budget into PMax amplified the problem and slid into C04 and C11.
case.C16.title: Leads lost to slow response
case.C16.summary: Lead volume is good but replies are late. Prospects lose interest and go elsewhere.
case.C16.symptoms: Lead count is good, demo and trial rates low, and 'unreachable' notes pile up.
case.C16.hint: A lead's value decays by the hour. Fix response speed first, then add volume.
case.C16.correct.outcome: You set up an auto first reply and response slots. CAC fell at the same spend.
case.C16.wrong.outcome: Buying more leads wasted spend; unanswered leads decayed.

events.cpc-inflation.text: Competition and demand temporarily pushed CPC and CPM up.

events.policy-warning.text: The platform sent a policy warning about one of your ads. Review your content.
events.algorithm-change.title: Algorithm change
events.algorithm-change.text: The platform updated its algorithm; delivery may wobble for a while.
events.measurement-loss.title: Measurement loss
events.measurement-loss.text: A browser or privacy change reduced observed conversions.
events.competitor-move.title: Competitor move
events.competitor-move.text: A competitor raised ad spend or launched a new campaign.
events.review-crisis.title: Review crisis
events.review-crisis.text: A negative review is spreading. Respond and fix the problem.
events.viral-share.title: Viral share
events.viral-share.text: A post got unexpected attention; organic leads briefly spiked. Keep response times up.
events.fx-shock.title: FX shock
events.fx-shock.text: The lira lost value; USD-denominated tools and ad costs rose.
events.abmahnung.title: Abmahnung
events.abmahnung.text: A cease-and-desist (Abmahnung) arrived from a competitor or association, with lawyer fees and penalty risk. Game commentary, not legal advice.
events.tcpa-complaint.title: TCPA complaint
events.tcpa-complaint.text: A person complained about an unsolicited call or text. Game commentary, not legal advice.
events.einvoice-deadline.title: E-archive / E-Rechnung deadline
events.einvoice-deadline.text: An e-invoicing mandate date is near. It creates compliance work but also a sales opening with salons. Dates come from markets/*.json and may be unverified.
events.holiday-density.title: Holiday density
events.holiday-density.text: A public holiday or festival period shifts demand and buying behaviour.
